idiom_name: noninstantiable utility class of static methods + capability interface (Collections/Objects style)
implementation_notes: Java has no free functions, so the servant is a class whose only purpose is the service: a noninstantiable utility class (private constructor, all-static methods - Effective Java item 4, and the shape of java.util.Collections, Arrays, Objects) whose methods take the serviced object as a parameter, or an ordinary servant object when the behaviour carries policy state or must be injected for tests. The capability the servant requires is a small interface declared on the servant's side (Movable, Comparable, Comparator) and implemented by the serviced classes; Comparable/Comparator are the JDK's own version of this contract, and Collections.sort(list, comparator) is a servant that serves any List. When you own the serviced interface, a default method can absorb the servant entirely, which is the modern Java alternative to a utility class.
pitfalls: A static servant cannot be substituted: tests cannot mock it and every call site is hard-wired, so move to an injectable servant object as soon as the behaviour touches I/O, the clock or configuration.

Widening the serviced class's public API (getters and setters) for the servant's benefit weakens its invariants: any caller can now drive the object through the same door, and the class drifts into an anemic data holder.
Static state in a servant is process-wide: a utility class that caches or accumulates per-call data becomes a shared mutable global with no lifecycle.
sources: Oracle, java.util.Collections (Java SE 23) - a class consisting exclusively of static methods that operate on or return collections, i.e. the JDK's servant for the collection interfaces; https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/23/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Collections.html

Oracle, java.util.Objects (Java SE 23) - static utility methods operating on objects, the noninstantiable utility-class shape in the JDK; https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/23/docs/api/java.base/java/util/Objects.html
Java Design Patterns, Servant Pattern in Java - servant + capability interface (Servant/Royalty) structure and applicability; https://java-design-patterns.com/patterns/servant/
